The Mauryan Empire came to an end around 185 BCE when the last Mauryan ruler Brihadratha was assassinated by his commander-in-chief Pushyamitra Sunga. Pushyamitra founded the Sunga Dynasty, which ruled large parts of North India from 185 BCE to 73 BCE. The Sungas revived Brahmanical traditions while continuing several Mauryan administrative institutions.
Hence, the correct answer is

s: Which religion did King Kharavela patronise?
x:
King Kharavela was the most celebrated ruler of the Mahameghavahana (Chedi) dynasty of Kalinga. Most of the information about him comes from the famous Hathigumpha Inscription at Udayagiri near Bhubaneswar. Kharavela was a devout follower and patron of Jainism. He repaired Jain monasteries, supported Jain monks and promoted the spread of Jainism throughout his kingdom. According to the Hathigumpha inscription, he also brought back the sacred Jina idol that had earlier been carried away by a Nanda ruler of Magadha. Although he patronised Jainism, Kharavela followed a policy of religious tolerance and extended support to followers of other faiths as well.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).
